newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX GASOLINE ONLY BAR TO MORE CRUDE GAINS.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX GASOLINE ONLY BAR TO MORE CRUDE GAINS.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - Aug 12 -------------- * Crude must get through resistance at $19.75 and head towards $20, though the latter could depend on support for gasoline.
* Medium-term charts still look okay for the crude bulls.
* Heating oil underpinned by double bottom support at $54.25 with ACCESS price action extending this to a near triple bottom.
NYMEX crude and product futures are expected to edge higher today with all contracts finding good trendline support and momentum indicators in oversold territory.
However, analyst said much depends on gasoline which remains volatile to the downside as the peak season draws to a close, though heating oil could be taking up the baton.

Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report, "WTI must get through resistance at $19.75 and head towards $20 though the latter could depend on support in the gasoline marketwhich still looks decidedly shaky".
"Overall, it's a case of 'wait and see' in the short term but the medium term charts still look okay for the crude oil bulls".

Parallel trendline support, drawn from last Friday's $19.49 low at the same angle and parallel to the bullish trend seen from July 22 to August 5 on the spot month continuation chart, comes in at around $19.60 today.
The $19.75 daily high/low resistance marker was already being attacked in ACCESS trading leaving the door open for a move to $20 with little further resistance in between.

Fenella Graham at MeesPierson said, "Gasoline remains the major influence and we keep a close eye on volatility here as the preparation is leaning on the negative and the season heads towards its close".
However, analysts expected some short-covering ahead of the APIs to help halt gasoline's recent slide.

"The bearish downtrend in the product continues, but oversold RSI's and the holding of support at the 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement level indicates the market may be in for some short-covering," said Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore.
He said this could happen tonight and tomorrow if the APIs can produce another draw down in stocks like last week.
Heating oil is seen underpinned by double bottom support on the spot month chart from Friday and Monday's $54.25 low with ACCESS price action extending this to a near triple bottom.
This support also lies on key a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement level and analysts say this combined with oversold technical indicators offers the chance of a good buying opportunity.
"Also we are starting to get into the season of talking about Winter an added psychological supportive factor not to be ignored," Tom James said.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
